# Chroma unit-test ephemeral tenant/database isolation (UNIT_TEST_MODE)

## Context

Split from #12331 (unit-test store isolation). #12331 ships the daemon-spec `os.tmpdir()` isolation + the `purgeTestCollections` reclaimer (parts 1 + 3). This ticket is the deferred **part 2**: by-construction ephemeral isolation of the unit-test ChromaDB namespace.

## The Problem

Under `UNIT_TEST_MODE`, the memory-core config names test collections `test-memory-*` / `test-session-*` (`config.template.mjs:119-120`), but they still land in the **same** `default_tenant`/`default_database` as production. `afterAll` cleanup handles the happy path; interrupted/`Ctrl-C`/CI-cancel runs and bare-`npx` bypasses leak orphans into the prod namespace (the 1,281 backlog #12331's purge clears). The purge is a *reclaimer*, not *prevention* — orphans re-accumulate between runs.

## The Fix

Route the unit-test Chroma client to an isolated **tenant/database** (chroma multi-tenancy) under `UNIT_TEST_MODE`, so test collections never enter `default_tenant`/`default_database` and the whole test namespace is droppable wholesale. Prod path stays `default_tenant`/`default_database` (unchanged). This is the chroma analogue of the graph store's already-correct `:memory:` isolation (`config.template.mjs:112`).

## The Architectural Reality

- `ai/services/memory-core/managers/ChromaManager.mjs:82` — `new ChromaClient({host, port, ssl: false})`; add `tenant`/`database` under `UNIT_TEST_MODE`. The test db must be ensured-to-exist on connect (chroma 3.x admin/create-database API) — confirm the exact mechanism (tenant vs database vs throwaway persist-dir) against chromadb 3.3.1 at implementation.
- `ai/scripts/maintenance/purgeTestCollections.mjs` (from #12331) — once isolation lands, the purge can drop the whole test tenant/db instead of enumerating `test-*` names.
- **Sensitive surface:** this mutates the prod chroma connect path (UNIT_TEST_MODE-guarded). Deserves its own focused PR + careful prod-regression verification (the reason it was split from #12331).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1 — Under `UNIT_TEST_MODE`, test collections resolve to a tenant/database distinct from `default_tenant`/`default_database` (statically verifiable); no test run — including crashed/`npx`-bypassed — can create collections in the prod namespace.
- [ ] AC2 — Prod path unchanged (`default_tenant`/`default_database`); prod-wipe guards (`DestructiveOperationGuard`, FATAL `UNIT_TEST_MODE` guard) intact.
- [ ] AC3 — `purgeTestCollections` can drop the whole test namespace (in addition to the name-pattern path).

## Related
- Parent: #12331 (parts 1 + 3 shipped)
- Resolves-by-prevention (with #12331's purge-run): #12143, #12180

* test(ai): assert engines.chroma.database in the Tier-1 shape contract (#12335)

The strict toEqual shape contract for engines.chroma in config.template.spec.mjs
must include the new database leaf. Full-suite CI surfaced this (1 failed / 2625
passed); the targeted single-spec runs masked it because they didn't exercise the
config-shape contract test.

* fix(ai): fail-closed guard — refuse production Chroma database under UNIT_TEST_MODE (#12335)

PR #12397 cycle-1 review surfaced a real AC1 escape hatch: under UNIT_TEST_MODE an
inherited NEO_CHROMA_DATABASE=default_database override still resolved the unit client
to the production database. resolveChromaClientConfig now throws fail-closed when
UNIT_TEST_MODE is active and the resolved database is the production name, so the
manager cannot construct or connect into the production namespace from a unit run.
Production NEO_CHROMA_DATABASE override behavior is intact outside UNIT_TEST_MODE.

- 2026-06-12T03:42:33Z @tobiu referenced in commit `21d502e` - "fix(agentos): B4-safe debug activation via setEnvOverride (#12889) (#12952)

Replace the ADR-0019 B4 write-class consumer mutation of the read-only reactive Provider singleton (`<Config>.data.debug = true` — the #12335/#12435 shared-instance-bleed hazard) with `<Config>.setEnvOverride('NEO_DEBUG', true)`, the Provider's sanctioned runtime env-override API, at the 4 remaining sites: runSandman, syncKnowledgeBase, migrateMemoryCore, ingestTenant.

The debug leaf is env-backed (NEO_DEBUG) but env resolution is bounded, not live-per-read (re-resolved only at construct/setEnvOverride/load), so a raw process.env set after construct would no-op; setEnvOverride validates, registers the override, and re-applies the env layer immediately. data.debug reads true after, so no read-back regression."

- 2026-06-14T13:36:17Z @tobiu referenced in commit `a3380ac` - "feat(ai): fail-build lint banning Class-A DB-path AiConfig mutation in tests (#13227) (#13228)

* feat(ai): fail-build lint banning Class-A DB-path AiConfig mutation in tests (#13227)

A test that writes aiConfig.{storagePaths|engines.chroma.database|collections|logPath} to
the shared AiConfig singleton is the orphan-bleed mechanism: the reactive set-trap routes
the assignment to the shared provider, so the next consumer reads the test DB (the #12335
incident; ADR-0019 §4 B4). The B4 lint was unshipped (#12451 covered only the A4
inline-process.env guard).

check-aiconfig-test-mutation.mjs flags these DB-path assignments in test/** (code only —
string + comment context excluded), grandfathering the current 22 offenders + an
aiconfig-mutation-ok escape marker, wired into lint-staged. Config-varying leaves (Class B)
and the broad lint are deferred pending the override-mechanism design.

Validated: 12/12 unit tests (regex, string/comment exclusion, escape marker, allowlist);
repo self-scan reports 0 new violations (22 grandfathered); a new violation exits 1.
Refs #12435, #12456.

* fix(ai): close bracket-literal bypass + add CI workflow for the test-mutation lint (#13227)

Addresses the REQUEST_CHANGES on #13228:

(1) Bracket-literal bypass — aiConfig["storagePaths"].graph / Memory_Config.data["collections"]
slipped the dot-only regex. Root cause: findDbPathMutations stripped all string contents before
matching, erasing the bracket KEY (itself a string). Replaced the strip pass with a codeMask: match
on the raw line, accept only when the aiConfig/Memory_Config root sits in code — so a string
bracket-key is detected while a fully-in-string pattern stays excluded. Regex extended to match dot OR
string-literal-bracket leaf access; computed keys (aiConfig[varName]) documented as out of a static
lint's reach.

(2) CI-gate framing — the check was lint-staged (pre-commit, --no-verify-bypassable) only. Added
.github/workflows/aiconfig-test-mutation-lint.yml (path-triggered on test/** + the script), a true
fail-build gate matching the config-template-ssot / skill-manifest lint pattern.

Validated: 14/14 unit tests (+ bracket positives, computed-key + Class-B-bracket negatives,
string/comment exclusion); repo self-scan 0 new violations; node --check clean.

* fix(ai): drop commander so the test-mutation lint workflow runs without npm install (#13227)

The new aiconfig-test-mutation-lint CI workflow runs `node check-aiconfig-test-mutation.mjs`
without an npm install step (the dependency-free pattern the other lint workflows follow), so
the `commander` import failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND at the exact head. Replaced commander
with a minimal built-in argv parse (positional [files...] + --quiet); no behavior change, and
the lint is now dependency-free.

Validated: only node: imports remain; node --check clean; self-scan 0 new violations;
file-arg + --quiet parse correctly; 14/14 unit tests green."
- 2026-06-18T19:54:03Z @neo-opus-vega cross-referenced by PR #13468
- 2026-06-20T20:14:17Z @neo-opus-ada referenced in commit `d982826` - "feat(ai): fail-closed test-write isolation guard for the graph storage (#13639)

Graph-node writes had no production guard — GraphService.upsertNode only validated
the id. So a bare `npx playwright test` (which, unlike playwright.config.unit.mjs,
never sets UNIT_TEST_MODE, so storagePaths.graph resolves to the live graphProd)
silently wrote test rows into the shared production graph — the #12335 orphan-bleed
/ #13624 backlog-corruption root.

The destructive twins (Store.guardProductionWipe, chromaDeleteCollection) guard by
prod-TARGET, which is correct only for destructive ops; inserts are constant in
production, so a target refusal would break the live runtime. This guard therefore
keys on the test CALLER, not the target.

SQLite.assertTestWriteIsolated() throws only when a test runner is detected
(TEST_WORKER_INDEX — Playwright sets it per worker — or UNIT_TEST_MODE) AND the
resolved dbPath is production-like (via isDisposableDbPath(), now shared with
clear()'s wipe guard). Config-independent — fires "regardless of harness or config
state" (the 2026-05-17 Chroma-incident lesson). Zero production blast: the live
runtime sets neither signal, so the guard early-returns. Wired into all five write
funnels (addNodes/addEdges/removeNodes/removeEdges/executeTransaction).

Tests: SQLiteWriteGuard.spec.mjs (6, full branch coverage via injected dbPath/env +
a wired-funnel integration). No false-positives/regressions across the graph +
memory-core write specs (59 passed, 0 failed). Axis-3 of #13624 (graph integrity).
Picked up per @neo-opus-grace's #13624 sunset handover."
